options.text: A lunar eclipse — Earth is blocking sunlight from reaching the Moon.
A total lunar eclipse — Earth's shadow need only touch any part of the Moon.
A lunar eclipse — the Moon looked round and bright before the shadow arrived.
A lunar eclipse — the Moon is blocking sunlight from reaching Earth.

stem:
Neil watches a full Moon darken as a curved shadow crosses its disc. His teacher says Earth's shadow is falling on the Moon.

Which claim correctly describes what is happening?

teacher.key_rationale: A lunar eclipse occurs when Earth blocks sunlight from reaching the Moon and Earth's shadow falls on the Moon. Totality needs the Moon fully in shadow; a round bright Moon beforehand is not the cause; the Moon blocking sunlight from Earth is a solar eclipse.
